transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I came in because... well, I honestly just can't see my carpentry studio, or my life for that matter, getting back on track anymore. It just feels like no matter how hard I work, or... or what kind of payment plan they put in front of me, it's not going to make a difference. I'm just at a dead end with it all.
Have you ever experienced a period like this in the past where you felt this low or hopeless for weeks at a time?

I'm not really sure. I mean... I don't remember a specific time in the past where I felt exactly like this for weeks at a time. I've had rough patches, sure, but... nothing really comes to mind that was quite like what I'm dealing with right now.
Was there a specific event or change in your life that happened shortly before you started feeling this way?
Yeah... it was when I took on the mortgage for the studio. That was a little over two years ago. I guess it's been about two years and two months now. That's when this all really started.
Have you felt this way every single day for the past two years, or have there been periods where you felt like yourself again?

I don't think I've had any time where I felt like my old self, no. It's... it's pretty much been every single day. I mean, maybe some days I'm just working and not thinking about it quite as much, but... the feeling is always there. I haven't really had a break from it since I signed those papers.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any consistent changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep?

Not really, no. I mean... I still eat about the same as I always have. And my sleep... I guess my sleep hasn't really changed much either. I haven't noticed any real differences with either of those, honestly.
Over these past two years, have you felt a persistent sense of inadequacy or low self-esteem?

Yeah, I'd say so. It's... it hits me hardest when I'm working. Like, if a joint doesn't line up perfect, or if I end up missing a bid deadline for a job, I don't just think, you know, "Oh, I made a mistake." I start thinking I'm just a lousy carpenter. I start telling myself that maybe I had no business trying to run my own studio in the first place. It just feels like I'm not good enough to be doing this.
During these past two years, have you found that you still get enjoyment or pleasure out of the things you used to love doing?

Honestly, I still enjoy the things I used to. I mean... I still like watching football on the weekends, or just having a beer on the porch. That hasn't really changed. I haven't lost interest in that stuff, it's just... I guess I just feel weighed down while I'm doing them. But the enjoyment is still there.
